newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 14.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Friday's Daily Variety:

* "Star Wars" by News Corp's Twentieth Century Fox became the first film to surpass $400 million in domestic box office sales Thursday. The 1977 production also regained the crown as the all-time top-grossing film in North America, which it had ceded to "E.T." in 1982.

* The dollar value of domestic shipments of CDs, cassettes, vinyl and music videocassettes topped $12.5 billion in 1996 and represented a 2.2 percent improvement over the previous year's tally, according to year-end statistics released Thursday by the Recording Industry Assn. of America.

* Walt Disney's ABC Entertainment is looking to install a No. 2 executive under president Jamie Tarses, a post that has been vacant since last fall. The leading candidate, according to industry sources, is Robert Dweck, currently president of Kushner-Locke's TV division.

* Actor-comedian Adam Sandler has landed a seven-figure payday to star in and co-write "The Water Boy" by Disney's Touchstone Pictures. The comedy is about a socially inept water boy for a college football team whose innate football abilities are discovered by the new coach.

* Jon Lovitz has signed a pact with Walt Disney that includes an exclusive TV deal, a starring role in a feature film, and a production company on the Disney lot to develop films for Lovitz to produce and-or star in.
* Twentieth Century Fox head of physical production Duncan Henderson is seeking to get an independent production deal at the studio, Fox sources said. No replacement has been named.
